attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors geometrically represents the product of the magnitude of one vector and the projection of the other vector onto it. Specifically, for vectors **a** and **b**, the dot product **a · b** equals |a| |b| cos(θ), where θ is the angle between them. If the vectors are orthogonal (θ = 90°), cos(θ) = 0, so their dot product is zero, indicating no projection of one vector onto the other. When the dot product is negative, it means the angle between the vectors is greater than 90° but less than 180°, so the projection of one vector onto the other points in the opposite direction, reflecting a negative scalar projection.
